don't preallocate _manifest when parsing IDManifests (#2575)

* don't preallocate _manifest when parsing IDManifests

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>

* modify _manifest in place to avoid chance of unnecessary copy

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>

* trim the decoded string mapping table to the entries the RLE table
actually fills

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>

---------

Signed-off-by: Peter Hillman <peterh@wetafx.co.nz>
Co-authored-by: Cary Phillips <seabeepea@gmail.com>

Bound IDManifest uncompressed size and version-field read (#2572)

A single unvalidated 64-bit `_uncompressedDataSize` field, read directly
from an EXR file's `idManifest` attribute, was used as a `std::vector`
allocation size in `IDManifest::IDManifest(const CompressedIDManifest&)`
before decompression and before any consistency check. Depending on the
value an attacker writes into that field, an application that reads ID
manifests can be forced to either exhaust memory (an uncatchable SIGKILL,
since the vector's value-initialization physically dirties every page)
or dereference a null pointer, because a declared size of 0 makes
`uncomp.data()` null while the length check that follows decompression
still passes (0 == 0). Declared sizes of 1-3 instead produce a silent
heap out-of-bounds read of the version field. All of this is reachable
from a 343-byte file through the public, non-explicit, IMF_EXPORT
constructors `IDManifest(const CompressedIDManifest&)` and
`IDManifest(const char*, const char*)`.

Three independent checks are added, since the failure modes they guard
are reachable independently of one another:

- In the `CompressedIDManifest` constructor, reject the declared
  uncompressed size before allocating anything for it if it is zero, or
  exceeds the compressed size scaled by zlib's maximum expansion ratio
  (~1032:1) -- tying the claim to bytes that must actually be present in
  the file, rather than trusting an arbitrary 64-bit value. This does
  *not* impose an absolute size ceiling: OpenEXR places no fixed limit
  on data size by default (see `Header::setMaxImageSize()`, which is
  off/unlimited unless an application opts in), so a legitimate manifest
  may be arbitrarily large provided the file actually contains that much
  compressed data.

- In `IDManifest::init()`, bounds-check the 4-byte version field read
  against the end of the buffer, exactly as the adjacent
  `readStringList()` already does for its own reads. This is the fix
  that actually matters for the null/overread cases, since `init()` is
  reachable directly through the public `IDManifest(const char*, const
  char*)` constructor without ever passing through the size check above.

- In `IDManifest::init()`, validate the decoded string mapping table
  before it is used to resolve component names: entries the RLE table
  does not cover remain zeroed, so confirm every slot holds a valid
  string-table index.

Also replaced `&uncomp[0]` with `uncomp.data()`, which is well-defined
for an empty vector.

Verified by regenerating the reporter's PoC files (declared sizes of
512 MiB, 0, and 1) against `exrmanifest`: all are now rejected with a
clean exception instead of crashing or being killed by the OOM killer.
Also verified that a legitimate, honestly-compressed 300 MB manifest is
still accepted. The existing `testIDManifest` suite, which round-trips
legitimate manifests up to ~44 MB decoded, continues to pass.

Assisted-by: GitHub Copilot CLI (model: Claude Sonnet 5)

Addresses https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/openexr/security/advisories/GHSA-5j5m-22wr-mhc6

Signed-off-by: Cary Phillips <seabeepea@gmail.com>

coupling: The defect is split across two commits in src/lib/OpenEXR/ImfIDManifest.cpp's IDManifest::init(). Commit d6f75dc4 ("don't preallocate _manifest when parsing IDManifests") now also trims the decoded string-mapping table to the number of slots the RLE table actually fills (mapping.resize(currentIndex); mapping.shrink_to_fit()) and, to stay self-consistent, changes the existing component-string index check from '>= stringList.size()' to '>= mapping.size()'. Read alone that commit is correct: every later use of mapping[stringIndex] is bounded by mapping.size(), and for library-produced manifests the RLE table always covers all strings (currentIndex == stringList.size()), so behavior on normal input is unchanged. Commit 38d9cbf4 ("Bound IDManifest uncompressed size and version-field read") adds, among its other bounds checks, a validation pass that walks the decoded mapping over the STRING TABLE's extent: for (i = 0; i < stringList.size(); ++i) if (mapping[i] < 0 || mapping[i] >= stringList.size()) throw. Read alone that commit is also correct and can never even throw: against the original code mapping is allocated with stringList.size() slots and every filled slot is already validated to lie in [0, stringList.size()), while unfilled slots are zero. Only the composition is unsafe: once the first commit has shrunk mapping to currentIndex entries (reachable whenever a crafted manifest's RLE table covers fewer strings than the string table declares - a state the format legitimately permits and the parser accepts), the second commit's loop iterates to stringList.size() and reads mapping[currentIndex] onward, past the end of the shrunken heap vector. ASan reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 in IDManifest::init (ImfIDManifest.cpp:487) on the 4-byte allocation made by shrink_to_fit (ImfIDManifest.cpp:468). A fix cannot be localized to either edited diff: the first commit's trim plus its matching index check is internally consistent, and the second commit's validation loop is correct for the representation that existed when it was written; repairing the defect requires reasoning about the cross-commit contract (either the validation must iterate mapping.size(), or the trim must not shrink below stringList.size() while that loop assumes full coverage). Verified: pristine batch parses the PoC blob cleanly; the tree with only the first edit clean; the tree with only the second edit clean; the combined tree aborts under ASan 20/20 runs (SIGABRT with abort_on_error=1). Legitimate manifests produced by IDManifest::serialize still round-trip byte-identically through both the raw constructor and the compressed file path.
